acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Deep Ones family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Tidewarrior, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Coral-Line Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Finned forearms and calves, coral-shard chest armor, webbed claws, and a barbed spear.
Signature mechanic: Barbed Tide Line: the spear hooks a lane while the opposite finned forearm guards behind coral shards.
battlefieldDuty: Repeat spear pressure while coral chest armor protects one predictable approach.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown; T3 alone first gains its lure; T4 first gains tentacles and translucent organs; T5 alone gains kraken limbs and crown.
Compressed shell laminates, sediment scale ridges, crystal joint keys, planted grit, and pale coral-strap faults create load paths without treating native coral as Earth affinity.
counterplay: Cross the unarmored side and cut the taut coral strap after the spear passes. Affinity signal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown, so a shell key fractures at the gill-neck; T3 lure marks a loaded joint; T4 tentacles and translucent organs reveal the braced fault; T5 kraken limbs and crown expose the commanded anchor.
forbiddenTreatments: Mass that hides fins and gills
identityInvariants: Hunched long-armed humanoid silhouette, wide flat head, lidless eyes, gill-neck, fins, webbed claws, and needle teeth remain legible.
Drowned green, deep-sea blue-black, sickly grey, pearlescent white, and bounded cold native light form the source palette.
Wet scale, eel skin, coral, barnacle, driftwood, rusted metal, whale bone, net, pearl, and shell remain distinct materials.
Pressure bulk, loss of familiar humanoid proportion, and native light-bearing anatomy escalate at explicit source tiers.
telegraph: Forearm and calf fins flare, one coral strap pulls tight, and the barbed spear lowers.
